datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: Section 6: 'The first set represents culturally-grounded and original prompts.' Section 2.2.1: 'This task facilitates the inclusion of human-generated organic content by allowing annotators to submit original prompt-completion pairs in their language... aims to encourage annotators to submit fresh samples that are representative of their language, culture, literature, history, and region.'

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: Section 6: 'We separate a curated subset of 200 Dolly prompts... We automatically translate the prompts with NLLB into 101 languages.' dolly-human-edited is post-edited from the same English-sourced machine translations.

details.aya-human-annotated: Original prompts written by fluent speakers in 7 languages, representing their language, culture, literature, history, and region. Section 6: 'The first set represents culturally-grounded and original prompts.'

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: aya-human-annotated: fluent speakers of each language (community volunteers). dolly-machine-translated: no native speakers involved (machine translation). dolly-human-edited: 'natively proficient or professionally proficient' annotators (Appendix F.1). Overall: mixed across the three subsets.

annotator_workforce.compensation_details: aya-human-annotated: No financial compensation; volunteers motivated by community, identity, and social justice (Section 7). dolly-human-edited: Professional annotators paid 30 CAD per hour (Appendix F.1).
annotator_workforce.evidence: Section 7: 'The motivations of contributors were not based on financial remuneration but on ideals of community, identity, and social justice.' Appendix F.1: 'The annotators were paid 30 CAD per hour.' Demographics for Aya community volunteers reported in Figure 3 (age, gender distribution). For dolly-human-edited annotators: 'We do not ask any annotators to share or report any of these statistical pieces of information in a formal way.'

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: 2 of 3 subsets (dolly-machine-translated and dolly-human-edited) are derived from English Dolly prompts. The paper explicitly acknowledges this limitation: 'some prompts, even when translated correctly, might still not transfer well into other languages—which is the main difference between a translated English-centric set like this and an evaluation set originally written in each target language like aya-human-annotated.' The aya-human-annotated subset (7 languages) is the only fully non-English-centric component. The paper recommends pairing translated sets with aya-human-annotated or dolly-human-edited for more reliable evaluation.

geographic_representation.evidence: Figure 4: 'more than half of all contributions for the Aya project came from Asia with 58.8%, followed by the African region with 27.4%. Europe, Latin America, and other regions account for the remaining 13.8% of the contributions.' The evaluation suite covers 101 languages spanning multiple continents but is concentrated in languages with NLLB/mT5 support. Figure 2 shows contributors from 119 countries with India having the highest number (346/2,997).
